flashcards.front: What is the difference between an unconfined and a confined aquifer?
flashcards.back: An unconfined aquifer lies directly below the permeable topsoil and connects with surface water; a confined aquifer is sealed between two impermeable rock/clay layers under high hydrostatic pressure.
flashcards.key_takeaway: Confined aquifers provide deep, protected groundwater reserves accessed via deep tube wells.

flashcards.front: What role do villi play in the small intestine?
flashcards.back: Villi are tiny, finger-like projections lining the inner wall of the small intestine that immensely increase surface area for nutrient absorption into blood vessels.
flashcards.key_takeaway: Villi maximize nutrient transfer efficiency into the circulatory system.

flashcards.front: How is Mechanical Advantage (MA) calculated for simple machines?
flashcards.back: MA = Load Force / Effort Force. An MA > 1 means the machine multiplies human effort to lift heavier loads.
flashcards.key_takeaway: Simple machines reduce required effort force by increasing distance or direction.

flashcards.front: What occurs during the Summer Solstice in the Northern Hemisphere (June 21)?
flashcards.back: The Northern Hemisphere is tilted at its maximum angle (23.5 degrees) toward the Sun, resulting in the longest day and shortest night of the year.
flashcards.key_takeaway: Solstices mark extreme seasonal light disparities.
